title: Ready-To-Drink Cocktails Move Into India's Deepavali Party Season
excerpt: India's RTD alcohol market crossed $200 million in 2025 and is growing faster than the global category, and this festive season global brands are putting pre-mixed cocktails — in flavours including jamun — into house parties in Goa, Bengaluru, Mumbai and Pune.
body:
• India's ready-to-drink (RTD) alcohol market crossed $200 million in value in 2025, registering 11 percent year-on-year growth, according to IWSR data cited by Mint.
  • Diageo India says the RTD category is growing 12 percent in volume versus last year, and launched Smirnoff ICE in Goa, Bengaluru and Mumbai on October 8, 2026, ahead of the festive season.
  • BuzzBallz, which debuted in Bengaluru in December 2025, has expanded into Maharashtra and Pune with four flavours created for India, including Jamun Mint Pop and Chili Guava Groove.
  • The category remains small next to beer and spirits, and state-by-state alcohol rules still decide where and at what price these drinks can be sold.

The cocktail at an Indian house party this Deepavali increasingly arrives already mixed. Ready-to-drink, or RTD, alcoholic beverages — pre-mixed products that can be consumed without any further mixing — are the format global drinks companies are pushing into India's festive season, and the numbers behind the push are now material. India's RTD alcohol market crossed $200 million in value in 2025, registering 11 percent year-on-year growth, according to market data cited by Mint from the international drinks consultancy IWSR and reported by Indian Food Times. Between 2022 and 2025, the category recorded a compound annual growth rate of 6 percent, compared with 3 percent globally, the same data showed.

Global brands timed their launches for the festivals

Diageo India launched Smirnoff ICE in India on October 8, 2026, rolling out first in Goa, Bengaluru and Mumbai, with plans to expand into additional markets ahead of the festive season. The launch has two expressions — Smirnoff ICE at 4 percent alcohol by volume and Smirnoff ICE MAX at 8 percent — in flavours including jamun, cranberry and citrus. In its launch announcement, Diageo said the ready-to-drink category is among the country's fastest-growing segments, increasing 12 percent in volume versus last year, and described the format as suited to casual outings, house parties and spontaneous plans with friends — the occasions that multiply around Deepavali.

"India is evolving as a new generation seeks out fresh formats, new flavours, more spontaneous ways to socialise and explore new drinking occasions."

— Ruchira Jaitly, Chief Marketing Officer, Diageo India

Diageo's entry puts it against Bacardi, which has built an established presence in India through its Breezer brand, according to Indian Food Times. The contest, that report said, is expected to centre on brand recognition, flavour innovation, retail distribution and pricing.

India-only flavours are part of the pitch

The other expansion under way is built around flavours made only for this market. BuzzBallz, the spherical-pack RTD cocktail brand, debuted in Bengaluru in December 2025 and launched in Goa in May, and is now available in Maharashtra and Pune, with a Mumbai launch scheduled for later this month, Beverage Daily reported. Its India portfolio has four flavours created exclusively for the market: Berry Lemon Squeeze, Strawberry Squeeze, Chili Guava Groove and Jamun Mint Pop. The brand's president, Jess Scheerhorn, pointed to the pack's 15 percent ABV and single-serve format, and said adult Indian consumers were ready for a more convenient way to enjoy cocktails. IWSR projects India's RTD category to grow at a 6 percent compound annual rate through 2034, ahead of the projected growth for several traditional beverage alcohol categories, Beverage Daily reported.

What has actually changed at the party

The practical change for a host is the removal of the mixing step. An RTD drink needs no spirits shelf, mixers or bartending, and it gives a guest a labelled, fixed-strength drink instead of a pour of unknown strength. For companies, the format also lets an established spirits brand such as Smirnoff extend into a different category and offer an alternative to conventional beer, spirits and cocktails, as Indian Food Times put it. That is the festive-season proposition both launches are selling: flavour-led, portable drinks for social occasions, in Indian flavours — jamun appears in both the Smirnoff ICE range and BuzzBallz's India-only line-up.

The limits are still real

None of the sources describes a mass market yet. The category remains relatively small compared with traditional beer and spirits, and growth alone does not settle whether new entrants will build repeat demand. Alcohol taxation, excise duties, licensing and distribution also vary by state in India, which affects pricing and availability and means a festive launch in Goa, Bengaluru and Mumbai does not automatically become a national one. What the 2026 festive season establishes is narrower and concrete: India's RTD market is growing at roughly twice the global category's recent rate, the world's large drinks companies are now launching into it in the weeks before Deepavali, and they are doing so with flavours formulated for Indian drinkers rather than imported unchanged.
